captions.instagram:
How does an RO water purifier work?

Your kitchen purifier pushes water so hard that it squeezes out of the salt, through a skin with no real holes. Take an RO purifier apart in 3D, flip osmosis backwards, and see where the other two litres go.

→ A home RO purifier is a row of filters, a pump and one very fine membrane.
→ Only water squeezes through the membrane. Salt and germs go down the drain.
→ Water sneaks through a membrane towards the salty side. That is osmosis.
→ Push harder than the osmotic pressure and the flow flips: reverse osmosis.
→ Unroll an RO cartridge: a membrane sheet with a skin a few hundred times thinner than a hair.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/roclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does an RO water purifier work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Your kitchen purifier pushes water so hard that it squeezes out of the salt, through a skin with no real holes. Take an RO purifier apart in 3D, flip osmosis backwards, and see where the other two litres go.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/roclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/roclear

In this video:
• A row of filters and one fine membrane. A home RO purifier chains a sediment filter, activated carbon, a booster pump, the RO membrane, a carbon polish, a UV lamp and UF fibres, a mineral cartridge and a storage tank.
• Osmosis, run backwards. Water on its own flows through a membrane towards the saltier side.
• No holes, just a very thin skin. The membrane is a polyamide skin about 0.1 to 0.2 micrometres thick, rolled round a tube.
• TDS: less is not always better. RO takes 1,000 ppm borewell water down to about 50 ppm.
• Most of the water goes down the drain. The rejected salt has to be washed away, so a typical home unit sends 2 to 3 litres to the drain for every litre you drink.
• UV kills, UF strains, neither desalts. UV-C light at 254 nm scrambles germs' DNA; the dose falls if the water runs faster or the lamp ages.
